dm.tag: dolma tag writes attribute files next to the documents: gopher_v1, c4_v1, pii_regex_with_counts_fast_v2. Nothing is dropped; every score is stored once.
dm.dedupe: dolma dedupe runs twice with Bloom filters: whole documents keyed on the text, then paragraphs (one per line). It only marks duplicates; the mixer acts on the marks.
dm.gopher: The mixer's exclude rules (written here to mirror datatrove's defaults; the toolkit ships taggers, not thresholds) drop 5 documents with Gopher rules. The reason shown is the first rule in the list that matches.

dm.bloom: 1 dropped as an exact duplicate document (d02). The near copy d03 is not a duplicate document, so it survives this step.
dm.spans: Span replacement deletes duplicate paragraphs and the PII spans. d03 shrinks to its one reworded sentence; d11 loses every paragraph (all seen in d10 first) and disappears; both IP addresses in d10 are replaced, documentation range included.
dm.out: 3 of 12 kept: d01, d10 (anonymised) and d03 reduced to one sentence.

summary: Both toolkits drop the same eight documents (seven bad ones and the exact copy), both lose d11, and both keep d01 and d10; but they disagree on the near copy: datatrove's MinHash removes d03 whole, while the Dolma toolkit's paragraph Bloom filter keeps its one new sentence as a document of its own. The rules also fire in a different order (a short banner falls to a repetition rule in datatrove, to the word count in Dolma), the PII regexes differ (datatrove keeps a non-global IP, Dolma replaces every IPv4 pattern), and paragraph dedup depends on order: d11 vanished only because d10 came first. Same input, same rules on paper, three different outputs in the details.
